rows.title: [Feature] Add search pets by name screen
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

Add a new screen that allows users to search for pets by name, similar to the existing "Find Owners" functionality.

## Motivation

- Currently there is no way to search for a pet directly by name; users must first find the owner and then browse their pets.
- A dedicated pet search screen would improve usability when the pet name is known but the owner is not.
- Aligns the pet entity with the same search UX pattern already established for owners.

## Proposed Solution

1. **New Thymeleaf template** (`templates/pets/findPets.html`) with a search form and results list/table.
2. **New controller** endpoint(s) in a `PetController` (or extend existing controller) to handle `GET /pets/find` and `GET /pets` with a `name` query parameter.
3. **New repository method** `findByNameContainingIgnoreCase(String name)` (or equivalent Spring Data query) in `PetRepository`.
4. **Navigation link** added to the main layout so users can access the pet search screen.
5. **Accessibility**: the new page must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA (keyboard navigation, visible focus, proper labels, contrast, landmarks, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A "Find Pets" link is available in the main navigation menu
- [ ] Users can search for pets by entering a full or partial pet name (case-insensitive)
- [ ] An empty search returns all pets
- [ ] Search results display pet name, birth date, type, and owner name
- [ ] Clicking a result navigates to the pet's or owner's detail page
- [ ] The page is accessible (landmarks, labels, keyboard support, contrast)
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover the new controller and repository methods
- [ ] Works with H2 (default), MySQL, and PostgreSQL profiles

## Alternatives Considered

- Extending the existing owner search to also filter by pet name — rejected because it conflates two different search intents.

## Additional Context

The implementation should follow the same patterns used by the existing "Find Owners" feature (`OwnerController`, `findOwners.html`, `ownersList.html`).

rows.title: Owner.addPet silently ignores persisted pets and PetValidator lacks name length check
rows.excerpt:
The Owner.addPet(Pet pet) method in Owner.java contains a logic bug where it only adds a pet to the owner's pet list if pet.isNew() returns true (i.e., the pet has no ID). This means that any persisted pet (one that already has a database ID assigned) is silently ignored when added to an owner.

This bug manifests in PetController.updatePetDetails() where the else branch calls owner.addPet(pet) for a pet with an existing ID. Since the pet is not new, the call silently does nothing, and the pet is never associated with the owner.

Expected behavior: The addPet method should add any pet that is not already present in the owner's pet list, regardless of whether the pet is new or persisted.

Actual behavior: Only pets with a null ID are added. Pets with a valid ID are silently dropped.

Additionally, the PetValidator class lacks a name length validation check. The Pet entity inherits from NamedEntity which has a @Column(length=30) constraint, but the validator does not enforce this at the form validation level. This means names exceeding 30 characters pass validation but fail at the database level with a hard-to-debug constraint violation.

Steps to reproduce:

Create an Owner instance
Create a Pet instance and assign it an ID (e.g., pet.setId(5))
Call owner.addPet(pet)
Observe that owner.getPets() returns an empty list
Acceptance criteria:

Owner.addPet adds persisted pets that are not already in the list
Owner.addPet does not add duplicate pets
PetValidator rejects pet names longer than 30 characters
All existing tests continue to pass
New unit tests cover the fixed behavior
Word count: ~240 RULE 7 status: PASS

rows.title: Documentation: Improve documentation across classes
rows.excerpt:
## Summary
This PR improves documentation across three core classes in the PetClinic application as part of the sustainable coding practices evaluation for SE754 Assignment 5.

## Problem
Manual review and SonarQube feedback showed that several important classes in the owner and vet areas were under-documented. While the code was functional, the intent of the domain objects and controller flows was not immediately clear to readers, especially around model preparation, pet ownership rules, and veterinarian specialty handling.

The `Owner` domain model, `PetController`, and `Vet` model each contain logic that benefits from clearer class-level and method-level documentation. Without that context, future contributors have to infer behavior from implementation details rather than from the API contract.

## Changes
- Expanded the class-level documentation in `Owner.java` to explain its role as the core owner entity and its relationship to pets
- Added method-level documentation in `PetController.java` to clarify:
  - model attribute preparation
  - request binding
  - validation flow
  - pet create/update handling
- Improved the class and method documentation in `Vet.java` to explain:
  - specialty management
  - the read-only sorted view exposed to callers

## Sustainability Impact
Better documentation reduces cognitive load for future maintenance work. These classes are part of the main application flow, so clearer comments and Javadoc help new contributors understand why the code exists, not just what it does.

This improves long-term maintainability by:
- reducing onboarding friction for new contributors
- making controller and domain behavior easier to reason about
- lowering the risk of incorrect future modifications
- improving overall code readability and maintainability

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Owner.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/Vet.java`

rows.title: Add owner pet name fields validations
rows.excerpt:
Fixes #2554

## Issue

Owner and Pet name validation was incomplete, allowing numeric-only values (for example: `12345`) to be submitted and persisted.

## Analysis

* `PetValidator.java` existed, but its validation logic only checked for empty values and did not enforce meaningful name constraints.
* There was no dedicated `OwnerValidator.java`, which meant owner names relied only on basic persistence constraints.
* Name fields were effectively unrestricted in length beyond the database column definition. A 30-character maximum is more practical and aligned with expected usage.

## Changes Made

* Updated `PetValidator.java` to enforce:

  * Non-empty values
  * At least one alphabetic character
  * Maximum length of 30 characters

* Added `OwnerValidator.java` following the existing validator pattern used in the project to validate:

  * `firstName`
  * `lastName`

* Ensured custom validation integrates with existing Bean Validation (`@Valid`) without overriding entity-level constraints.

## Validation Rules

Both Owner and Pet names now:

* Must not be blank
* Must contain at least one letter
* Must be 30 characters or fewer

This prevents invalid numeric-only entries while keeping valid alphanumeric names supported.

## Testing

Tested locally across all affected flows:

* Creating a new Owner
* Updating an existing Owner
* Creating a new Pet
* Updating an existing Pet

Verified:

* Valid names are accepted
* Blank values are rejected
* Numeric-only values are rejected
* Overlength names are rejected

Evidence attached.

rows.title: Prevent duplicate pet creation with similar name for the same owner under concurrent requests
rows.excerpt: ## Summary This Pull Request resolves a concurrent race condition in the Spring PetClinic application that allows users to create duplicate pets with the same name (case-insensitive) under the same owner. ## Problem In a concurrent environment, if two requests are sent simultaneously to create a pet with the same name for the same owner, both checks succeed, bypassing the in-memory validation check and inserting duplicate pet records. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start the Spring Boot application locally. 2. Create an owner (or use an existing owner with no pet named `PRTESTPET`). 3. Send two concurrent `POST` requests to `/owners/{ownerId}/pets/new`, both using the pet name `PRTESTPET`. 4. Open the owner's details page. 5. Observe that both requests succeed and duplicate pets with the same name are created for the same owner. ## Root Cause The duplication validation is executed entirely in Java memory (using a check-then-act pattern: `owner.getPet(petName, false) != null`), and there is no database-level unique constraint or lock to serialize concurrent insert operations. ## Solution 1. **Database-Level Case-Insensitive Uniqueness Constraints**: - **H2**: Change the `pets.name` column type to `VARCHAR_IGNORECASE(30)` and add a unique constraint on `(owner_id, name)`. - **MySQL**: Add a unique constraint `UNIQUE (owner_id, name)`. - **PostgreSQL**: Add a unique functional index: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX unique_owner_pet_name ON pets (owner_id, LOWER(name));`. 2. **Immediate Persistence**: - Change `save()` to `saveAndFlush()` in [PetController.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java) to ensure SQL execution and trigger constraint violations within the try-catch block. 3. **Graceful Exception Translation**: - Update [PetController.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java) to catch `DataIntegrityViolationException`, verify if it is the specific `unique_owner_pet_name` violation, and translate it into a clean validation error on the name field. rows.title: Feature/pet registration
rows.excerpt:
Added Pet Registration section

Adds a standalone "Register Pet" flow, separate from the existing "Add Pet" button on an owner's page. Gives staff a direct way to register a pet without hunting down the owner's page first.

---

How it works

| Step | Route | What happens |
|------|-------|--------------|
| 1 | `GET /pets/register` | Search form — find owner by last name |
| 2 | `POST /pets/register` | Single match → straight to registration form. Multiple matches → pick-list |
| 3 | `GET /pets/register/{ownerId}` | Registration form for the selected owner |
| 4 | `POST /pets/register/{ownerId}` | Validates and saves (same duplicate-name / future-birthdate checks as the existing pet form) |

---

What's included

- `PetRegistrationController` (`org.springframework.samples.petclinic.pet`)
- 3 new templates — `registerSearchOwner.html`, `registerSearchResults.html`, `registerPet.html`
- New **Register Pet** nav item
- New `messages.properties` keys, translated for all supported locales

---

Design note

Reuses the existing `Owner` / `Pet` / `PetType` entities and `pets` table instead of adding a new one. The app already models pets as belonging to an owner — a second `Pet` class/table would've duplicated that and broken `schema.sql`.

No new dependencies. No schema changes.

---

Testing

 Verified the full search  - register - save flow manually
 ./mvnw clean test passes
